record_type_quote:
In the
present study, we re-examined the claim of Hung, Styles, and Hsieh (2017) that such
sound-shape mappings can occur before becoming aware of the visual stimuli. More precisely,
we replicated their first experiment in which congruent and incongruent stimuli (e.g., bouba
presented in a round or an angular shape, respectively) were rendered invisible through
continuous flash suppression.

targets.authors: Hung, S.-M., Styles, S. J., & Hsieh, P.-J.
targets.title: Can a word sound like a shape before you have seen it? Sound-shape mapping prior to conscious awareness.
targets.evidence_quote:
In the
present study, we re-examined the claim of Hung, Styles, and Hsieh (2017) that such
sound-shape mappings can occur before becoming aware of the visual stimuli. More precisely,
we replicated their first experiment in which congruent and incongruent stimuli (e.g., bouba
presented in a round or an angular shape, respectively) were rendered invisible through
continuous flash suppression.
targets.outcome_quote:
The results showed that congruent combinations, on average,
broke suppression faster than incongruent stimuli, thus providing converging evidence for
Hung and colleagues’ assertions.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors support the tested effect; smaller effect magnitude does not change the verdict.

targets.authors: Jiang, Y., Costello, P., & He, S.
targets.title: Processing of invisible stimuli: Advantage of upright faces and recognizable words in overcoming interocular suppression.
targets.evidence_quote:
The sole difference was that we used
the t-value and sample size reported by Jiang et al. (2007) to determine BFr0 (respectively,
5.53 and 10).
targets.outcome_quote:
In light of the large BF10 , one could therefore
conclude that there is compelling evidence for a face inversion effect, but of a more modest
magnitude compared with earlier studies (see also Stein et al., 2012).
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors support the tested effect; smaller effect magnitude does not change the verdict.

reasoning: Verified complete 23-page manuscript, title, all five authors and reference list. Primary experiment re-tests Hung et al. Experiment 1. The added control experiment also re-tests a specific published face-inversion finding and explicitly compares against Jiang et al. 2007 using their t-value and sample size. Stein et al. is contextual support for that effect, not a separately identified original protocol/result tested. The paper labels its own experiments main and control rather than numbering them. No own-data reproduction: reference-based Bayesian comparisons do not themselves constitute re-analysis of original participant data.
